column1: # tests/bats-suites.tsv — the canonical BATS suite table (single source of truth).
# Both bridges read this file rather than restating the list:
#   tests/test_bats_bridge.py    — pytest: one generated test per BATS @test case
#   tests/test_bats_unittest.py  — stdlib unittest: one case per suite FILE
# and tests/_bats_suites.py is the one parser they share.  Same arrangement as
# scripts/_module-list.sh is for the two shell loaders: a suite's membership and its
# timeouts are stated once, so the two runners cannot disagree about either.
# Columns, tab-separated, one suite per line:
#   pattern <TAB> marker <TAB> per_case_timeout_s <TAB> file_timeout_s
#   pattern              glob, relative to the repo root
#   marker               the pytest marker the pytest bridge applies to every case in
#                        the suite.  It must be registered in pytest.ini's markers=:
#                        an unregistered name is a collection error under
#                        --strict-markers, never a silent fallback.  The unittest
#                        bridge reads the column for its display only.
#   per_case_timeout_s   bounds ONE case (BATS_TEST_TIMEOUT)
#   file_timeout_s       bounds a whole-file run — a different quantity from the
#                        per-case figure, so the two must not be compared
# A new .bats file inside tests/unit/ or tests/integration/ joins its suite through
# the glob with no edit here.  A new SUITE (a new directory) needs a line, because its
# timeouts cannot be inferred from a glob.
tests/unit/*.bats
tests/tactical-console.bats
tests/tactical-console-fast.bats
tests/tactical-console-function-availability.bats
tests/integration/*.bats
